claims.statement: The Server database setting is a discriminated union of SQLiteConfig, OceanBaseConfig and SeekDBConfig keyed by kind, and a config without a kind is normalized to the SQLite default.

When no database URL is configured, the Server uses a SQLite file at powercontext.db inside the PowerContext data directory, which is POWERCONTEXT_HOME when set and the platform user-data path otherwise.
The default embedded seekDB location is a seekdb directory inside the PowerContext data directory, and a seekDB database config without a path is filled with that default.

The composition root opens SQLiteProfile for a SQLiteConfig, OceanBaseProfile for an OceanBaseConfig and SeekDBProfile for a SeekDBConfig, and raises a configuration error for any other database config.

The SQLite profile accepts only sqlite+aiosqlite URLs, defaults its model URL to in-memory storage, uses a StaticPool for non-persistent URLs, and sets the journal mode to WAL by default during warm-up under a per-file lock.

Embedded seekDB starts a local native instance through pylibseekdb, connects through an async MySQL-dialect socket, defaults to the powercontext database, and refuses to reuse legacy PowerContext tables in the test database unless the operator explicitly selects it.

The OceanBase profile requires a mysql+aoceanbase URL with a username, host, explicit port and charset utf8mb4, and it rejects any tenant whose ob_compatibility_mode is not MYSQL, except standalone seekDB identified by its version string.

Identity columns are declared with identity_string so that MySQL-family backends use utf8mb4_bin, and the OceanBase profile rejects existing schemas whose identity columns use another collation because create_all does not rewrite collations.

A database that already contains the pc_schema_revision control table is treated as managed: create_tables performs no DDL on it and raises unsupported_configuration when requested feature tables are missing.

On a managed database, Server startup only validates the processing schema, the current Atomic Memory projection and Topic Memory, while on an unmanaged database startup initializes storage, with SQLite taking BEGIN IMMEDIATE before bootstrap writes.

The Server migration chain is a linear sequence of revision files starting at the s1300 baseline (down_revision None) and continuing through s1400, s1401, s1402, v1_4_1_004, v1_4_1_005, v1_4_1_006, v1_5_0_001, v1_5_0_002, v1_5_0_003, v1_5_0_004 and v1_5_0_005, each declaring its down_revision, and Alembic records progress in the pc_schema_revision table.

The s1400 revision rebuilds candidate, profile, Artifact, processing-intent, Dream run and Topic budget tables by copying rows into temporary tables with explicit column lists, and it revokes the prior processing lease by advancing its generation and expiring it.

Legacy revision IDs s1300, r1400, s1400, s1401 and s1402 remain the stored identifiers, and the release-style names such as v1_4_1_001 are display aliases that do not create additional executable revisions.

The deployment runner requires an evidence directory for seekDB and OceanBase, requires single-host lock coordination for OceanBase, and accepts only a plain absolute SQLite file URL without credentials, host, port, query or in-memory option.

Plan is read-only and reports the state, pending revisions and backup availability; apply takes a local OS file lock, rechecks the plan, requires the accepted plan ID and maintenance confirmation, and writes completion evidence only after verification.

Admission of a managed SQLite snapshot accepts only a SQLiteMigrationRunner on the requested target with a separate absolute snapshot path, compares the recovery fingerprint before and after, opens the snapshot read-only, and returns only safe reason codes.
AsyncDatabase owns or attaches to one SQLAlchemy engine, repositories receive connections rather than owning the engine, and close drains active transactions before disposing only an owned engine.
Only SQLite busy or locked codes and MySQL-family lock-wait or deadlock codes are classified as rollback-safe transaction contention.

Candidate versions are stored in pc_candidate_versions keyed by scope, candidate and version, while pc_candidate_heads holds the mutable status and enforces by check constraint which result columns each pending, approved or rejected state may populate.

Artifact revisions are stored in pc_artifacts keyed by scope, family, artifact and revision, and pc_artifact_heads selects one revision through a composite foreign key while holding lifecycle, replacement and merge pointers.

Sources are stored in pc_sources keyed by scope, source type and source id with a per-scope unique journal position, and Artifact lineage links revisions to sources through a foreign key from pc_artifact_lineage_sources to pc_sources.

Processing state is persisted in tables keyed by binding_name and scope_id (pc_artifact_processing_pending and pc_artifact_processing_intents), a supervisor_group-keyed lease table and a singleton schema receipt, and none of the processing tables declares a foreign key, including to pc_scopes.
Handoffs have no dedicated table; the relational Handoff backend stores each Handoff lifecycle in the shared Artifact tables through ArtifactRepository.
Ordinary Server startup on managed storage checks readiness without repairing it, and a changed schema or inconsistent projection requires explicit maintenance rather than restart-based repair.

Focused tests cover read-only commands not creating databases, interruption at each revision boundary, checksum-conflict rejection, backup ordering, OceanBase tenant and seekDB legacy checks, and snapshot admission budget and source-change behavior.

When the selected database backend cannot start, the Server does not fall back to another backend: a missing pylibseekdb module raises SeekDBUnavailableError, and an OceanBase tenant that is neither MySQL mode nor standalone seekDB raises UnsupportedOceanBaseTenantError.

On SQLite the sqlite-vec extension is loaded, and vector Topic indexes and the Atomic Memory vector profile are attached, only when an embedding model is configured; without one Topic Memory keeps only its FTS index.
The Server rejects runtime.artifact_processing_role values other than 'all' for SQLite and embedded seekDB, so a background processing role requires the OceanBase backend.

pc_artifact_tags references its Artifact head through a cascading composite foreign key, and a check constraint limits each tag target to an artifact whose target id equals the artifact id or a memory_entry in the memory family.
pc_sources, pc_artifacts and the processing tables declare no foreign key to pc_scopes, so Scope partitioning on these tables is a logical key enforced by repository code rather than by the database.
Managed SQLite vector storage such as pc_artifact_vectors is created by registered revision resources rather than declared in tables.py.
For MySQL-family backends, unmanaged table creation skips tables that already exist and tolerates only verified index-name races (MySQL error 1061), re-raising any other index creation error.
